..
As of 700 AM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Breezy, sunny, and dry Fall weather continues this 
week.

The latest surface analysis revealed high pressure centered over the 
Great Lakes and a coastal low well offshore. Clouds associated with 
the low have moved offshore with clear skies across the local area.
Light winds overnight kept most sites from decoupling which has
resulted in a bit "milder" temps in the mid-upper 40s for most
inland areas as of 7 AM. Meanwhile, temps were in the mid-upper
50s along the coast.

The weather pattern remains largely stale over the next few days 
with a coastal low lingering well offshore and high pressure 
remaining centered to the NW of the local area through Thu. Highs 
will range from the upper 60s to lower 70s today through Thu with 
lows generally in the low-mid 40s inland and mid 50s along the 
coast. Wed night/Thu morning has the potential to be even cooler 
than currently forecast with mid-upper 30s possible across the 
Piedmont and typically cooler inland areas. As such, patchy frost is 
possible. Otherwise, clear skies continue through the week along 
with breezy conditions during the day. The only day where clouds 
could push inland appears to be Wed as the coastal low potentially 
nudges briefly closer to the coast. However, this looks to be short-
lived with clearing expected by Thu. Nevertheless, if clouds do 
materialize on Wed, temps would likely remain cooler, not getting 
out of the 60s. Winds remain northerly with gusts up to 20-25 mph 
possible inland and 25-35 mph possible along the coast today and 
Wed. Lighter winds are expected on Thu and Fri compared to earlier 
in the week. However, gusty conditions will remain possible mainly 
along the coast.

Cool, dry, and sunny conditions continue into the upcoming weekend 
as a strong area of high pressure (~1036 mb) builds into the region. 
The coolest day looks to be Sat with highs only in the lower 60s for 
most (mid 60s across far SE VA/NE NC). Additionally, given the 
strong high over the region, lows may drop into the mid-upper 30s 
(potentially cooler in spots) across inland areas Sat and Sun 
mornings with frost possible. However, the exact details regarding 
low temps those days is dependent upon the position of the high. If 
the high is centered farther north, temps will likely be milder and 
vice versa. Otherwise, models indicate that dry weather is likely 
here to stay for a while with no chance of rain over the next week 
(at least).


KEY MESSAGE 2...Prolonged onshore flow will lead to multiple
elevated tide cycles this week resulting in rounds of coastal
flooding. 

Prolonged onshore flow will produce tidal anomalies of 1 to 2 feet 
above normal astronomical tides. Fortunately, the region is 
currently in an astronomical neap tide cycle, which will help 
mitigate peak water levels. Even so, widespread minor to locally 
moderate coastal flooding is expected during high tides through mid 
to late week. The first high tide cycle of concern will be late
this afternoon/evening into tonight, with many sites across
adjacent to the Chesapeake Bay, tidal James River, and Atlantic
Ocean approaching or exceeding minor flood stage. Coastal Flood
Advisories remain in effect for Hampton Roads and areas along
the Atlantic Ocean. In addition, a Coastal Flood Advisory was
issued for the Middle/Northern Peninsulas. It should be noted
that areas along the tidal York River stay below minor flood
stage with this first round, thus advisories have not been
issued for these areas yet. 

Tidal levels are expected to gradually increase through 
Thursday, with higher levels possible each day. The tidal 
anomalies currently are not trending as high as previous 
forecasts. With the lower anomalies and lower NNE wind gusts, 
guidance has trended toward more widespread minor tidal 
flooding, rather than widespread moderate to locally major tidal
flooding. Coastal Flood Advisories will likely be need for the
eastern mid-upper Chesapeake Bay by Wednesday into the later 
portion of the week. There is also at least a signal that 
Bishop's Head may approach moderate flood stage Wednesday night 
or Thursday. Localized Coastal Flood Warnings may be needed 
later in this week for any localized moderate stage flooding, 
depending on trends.
